_meta.description: Full 30-question RAGAS evaluation, run twice on Kaggle GPU per kaggle/README.md, judge model qwen2.5:7b-instruct-q4_0, embeddings all-MiniLM-L6-v2. Real production runs (not the earlier n=2 local validation). Run 2 used max_workers=1 (fully serial) to test whether concurrency was causing the answer_relevancy NaN failure seen in Run 1 - it did not fix it, disproving that hypothesis (see LOG.md 'Phase 8 follow-up 2'). Full per-question response/context text is not stored here (some rows are very large, one pathologically so in Run 1 - see known_issues); scores are the complete real record for Run 1. Run 2's per-question detail was not captured (only console summary), only its mean_scores are recorded.
known_issues: answer_relevancy is NaN for all 30 questions in BOTH runs, including Run 2's fully-serial (max_workers=1) run - this rules out concurrency as the cause. A second hypothesis (response length/complexity) was also tested and ruled out via isolated local testing. Root cause still open as of this report - likely Kaggle-environment-specific (different Python/package versions than local dev, since requirements.txt doesn't pin exact versions). kaggle/diagnose_answer_relevancy.py exists to surface the real exception + package versions on Kaggle directly.

Faithfulness varied substantially between runs: 0.8679 (Run 1) vs 0.6555 (Run 2), a ~0.21 swing on the same 30-question set. LLM generation is non-deterministic, so some run-to-run variance is expected, but this magnitude means a single run's faithfulness score should not be cited as a fixed property of the system - see LOG.md and results/writeup.md Section 7.3.

Run 1 only: JPM-1's generated answer degenerated into a multi-thousand-character repetition loop (a known small/quantized-model failure mode). Corrupted faithfulness/context_precision for that row (both NaN); context_recall was unaffected since it doesn't depend on the generated response.

Custom '_id'/'_ticker' tracking columns added when building the RAGAS dataset were silently dropped by EvaluationDataset - Run 1's per-question rows below are matched to test-set IDs by position (processing order matches data/eval/ragas_test_set.json's question order), not by an explicit ID RAGAS preserved.

per_question.note: surprising - some claims in the response looked traceable to retrieved context on manual read; flagged as worth re-checking, see LOG.md
